title: Veritas unleashes deal spree across government tech, critical infrastructure
excerpt: Last week was busy for Veritas Capital. On Thursday, the New York-based private equity firm, which makes investments in government-adjacent and regulated ind...
content_html:
Esther Luz

Fri, August 7, 2026 at 5:16 PM EDT 2 min read

Last week was busy for Veritas Capital.

On Thursday, the New York-based private equity firm, which makes investments in government-adjacent and regulated industries, agreed to acquire Texas-based Saber Power Services, marking its third acquisition announcement in less than a week.

Days earlier, it agreed to acquire federal contractor Steampunk and environmental consultancy Trinity Consultants, and submitted a 914 pence-per-share proposal for London-listed Bodycote, valuing the industrial services company's equity at about £1.56 billion ($2.1 billion).

The bid places Veritas in a takeover contest with CVC Capital Partners, which proposed 915 pence per share. The bidders face a Sept. 2 deadline.

This dealmaking spree followed Veritas's July agreement to buy facilities management and engineering business BGIS.

Veritas has a big war chest to deploy. The firm, which has $54 billion in AUM, announced in February that it had raised $15.3 billion for its ninth flagship fund and related vehicles. The main fund closed at its $14.4 billion hard cap, coming in about 35% larger than its predecessor.

This flurry of deals stands out against a weaker overall buyout market. US private equity deal value fell 37.5% in Q2, and was down 23.9% year-over-year, according to PitchBook's Q2 2026 US PE Breakdown.

It also highlights investors' clamor to invest in businesses whose demand is backstopped by government policy, such as computer processing power, energy generation and traditional defense sectors.

The US defense budget has continued to grow, standing at $1.05 trillion in fiscal year 2026 and, pending congressional approval, could reach $1.5 trillion in fiscal year 2027.

The government has been courting PE and venture capital investment into the defense sector. In October, Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with KKR, Cerberus, Apollo Global Management and other buyout firms in talks to help finance a $150 billion overhaul of Army infrastructure.

This article originally appeared on PitchBook News

content_html_zh:
埃丝特·卢兹

美国东部时间 2026 年 8 月 7 日星期五下午 5:16 阅读 2 分钟

上周 Veritas Capital 非常忙碌。

周四，这家总部位于纽约的私募股权公司同意收购总部位于德克萨斯州的 Sabre Power Services，这是不到一周内的第三次收购公告。该公司主要投资与政府相关的受监管行业。

几天前，它同意收购联邦承包商 Steampunk 和环境咨询公司 Trinity Consultants，并提交了一份每股 914 便士收购伦敦上市公司 Bodycote 的提案，这家工业服务公司的股权估值约为 15.6 亿英镑（21 亿美元）。

此次出价使 Veritas 与 CVC Capital Partners 展开收购竞争，后者提出的收购价格为每股 915 便士。 竞标者面临9月2日的最后期限。

此次交易热潮是在 Veritas 7 月份协议收购设施管理和工程业务 BGIS 之后进行的。

Veritas 有大量资金可供部署。 该公司拥有 540 亿美元的资产管理规模，2 月份宣布已为其第九支旗舰基金和相关工具筹集了 153 亿美元。 该主基金的硬上限收盘价为 144 亿美元，比前任基金高出约 35%。

在整体收购市场疲软的背景下，这一系列交易显得格外突出。 根据 PitchBook 的 2026 年第二季度美国私募股权细分数据，第二季度美国私募股权交易价值下降 37.5%，同比下降 23.9%。

它还凸显了投资者热衷于投资需求得到政府政策支持的企业，例如计算机处理能力、能源生产和传统国防领域。

美国国防预算持续增长，2026财年达到1.05万亿美元，在国会批准之前，2027财年可能达到1.5万亿美元。

政府一直在吸引私募股权和风险投资进入国防部门。 10 月，陆军部长丹尼尔·德里斯科尔 (Daniel Driscoll) 和财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 与 KKR、Cerberus、阿波罗全球管理公司和其他收购公司进行了会谈，以帮助资助 1500 亿美元的陆军基础设施检修。
